ace_developer_workflow.overview: This mode guides you through developing IBM App Connect Enterprise (ACE) integration projects end-to-end: from understanding requirements, creating message flows, writing ESQL and Java, managing project structure, all the way through testing and validation.

critical_prerequisite.rule: ALWAYS activate the skill 'ace-bob' before creating or modifying ANY ACE artifact (message flows, ESQL, Java compute nodes, Maps, subflows, project files). The ace-bob skill provides the definitive xmi:type namespace prefixes and project structure rules that MUST be followed exactly.
Never guess xmi:type values — always verify from the ace-bob skill reference.
Never copy xmi:type values from existing example .msgflow files without verifying them against the ace-bob skill, as existing files may use outdated namespace prefixes.

steps.step: Read and understand the integration use case — protocol (HTTP/SOAP/MQ/File), message format (XML/JSON/CSV), and transformation requirements.
Identify the project type: Application, Library (.Lib), or Service (.Service).
Determine whether a shared library project is needed for reusable subflows/ESQL.
Identify all external systems: REST APIs, SOAP web services, databases, MQ queues, file systems, etc.
Clarify error handling requirements: what should happen on failure, timeout, and unexpected input.
Identify environment-specific configuration requirements (DEV/QA/UAT/PROD properties).
Design the high-level message flow: input node → processing nodes → output node.
Identify which built-in nodes are needed (see 2_node_reference.xml for guidance).
Plan shared subflows for cross-cutting concerns: error handling, auditing, logging.
Design ESQL modules for each Compute node, following naming conventions in 3_best_practices.xml.
Plan the Environment tree usage for passing state between nodes (avoid overuse of SHARED variables).
Design the error handling strategy: TryCatch node wrapping, catch terminal handling, and SOAP fault / HTTP error response generation.
Activate the ace-bob skill FIRST.
Create the ACE project structure (.project, .settings, application.descriptor or library.descriptor).
Create message flow files (.msgflow) — validate every xmi:type from ace-bob skill.
Create ESQL files (.esql) with the correct BROKER SCHEMA declaration.
Create Java files (.java) for JavaCompute nodes when needed.
Create environment-specific properties files (DEV.properties, QA.properties, UAT.properties, PROD.properties).
Follow all patterns documented in 3_best_practices.xml and 4_esql_patterns.xml.
Review each message flow for correct node connections (terminals must match).
Validate ESQL syntax: every CREATE COMPUTE MODULE must have matching END MODULE.
Verify BROKER SCHEMA declarations match the project package path.
Test using the SoapUI projects in the workspace (look for *_SOAPUI_Project folders).
Test error paths: submit invalid inputs, simulate backend failures.
Test timeout handling: verify timeout nodes and error responses work correctly.
Verify properties files have all required User-Defined Properties (UDPs).

type.name: Application
type.description: Deployable ACE application containing message flows and ESQL. Contains an application.descriptor file. Project nature: com.ibm.etools.msgbroker.tooling.applicationNature
type.file_extension: No suffix — use a plain descriptive name (e.g. WeatherAPI, not WeatherAPI.App)
type.naming_rule: DO NOT append '.App' to Application project names. Use a clean name such as 'WeatherAPI', 'OrderService', 'CustomerAPI'. The '.App' suffix is an old convention that must NOT be followed.

type.name: Library
type.description: Shared reusable components (subflows, ESQL procedures, schemas). Not directly deployable. Referenced by Application projects. Contains a library.descriptor file.

type.name: Service
type.description: WSDL-driven web service project. Contains WSDL, XSD, and generated message flows. Project nature includes service descriptor.

project_directory_conventions.convention: Source files live under a Java-style package path (e.g., com/company/esb/)
Properties files live under properties/ subdirectory
Generated files from WSDL live under gen/ subdirectory
WSDL and XSD files referenced by service projects live under RemoteFiles/
BAR files (deployment archives) live in the project root

testing_workflow.step: Locate the corresponding *_SOAPUI_Project directory for the service being tested.
Open the SoapUI project (*.xml file) in SoapUI or use the SOAP UI command line.
Configure the endpoint URL to match the DEV environment (from DEV.properties).
Run positive test cases: valid input, expected output.
Run negative test cases: malformed XML, missing fields, invalid values.
Verify error responses contain correct SOAP fault codes and messages.
Check the ACE system log for any exceptions or warnings.
Verify audit records are created if the flow uses audit subflows.
